Author: Chief Justice Bench: Chief Justice HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT JODHPUR S.B. Criminal Revision No. 182 / 1996 Anoop Singh Son of Shri Raghunath Singh Rajpurohit resident of Mathaniya District Jodhpur.
(At present lodged at Central Jail, Jodhpur)

sentences.text: __ HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE Judgment 04/07/2017
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: Perused the record of the trial Court and the decision of the learned Appellate Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 2. Exercising revisional jurisdiction I am not supposed to re- appreciate the evidence but if relevant evidence has been ignored or there are jurisdictional infirmities in the approach of the learned Trial Judge as well as, or the Appellate Court, I must exercise my revisional jurisdiction.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 3. Deciding the revision petition today I transpose myself to 06.05.1992.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text:
The petitioner was carrying on business from his shop when the Food Inspector Shri P.D.Arora (PW-1) picked up a sample of curd after purchasing the same from the petitioner and obtained the receipt (Exhibit- P5).
(2 of 4) [CRLR-182/1996]
4.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: The sample of curd was sent to the Public Analyst who, vide report Exhibit P-13, reported that milk fat content was 5.02%.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: Milk solids not fat content was 7.86%.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: Starch and cane sugar were absent.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: It was opined that the sample does not conform to the prescribed standards under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules 1955 because it contains about 13% of added water.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 5. From the record and specifically the report of the Public Analyst (Exhibit P-13) the position which emerges is that the Food Inspector never claimed to have enquired from the petitioner nor informed the Public Analyst that the curd was made from buffalo milk or cow milk.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 6. The defence witnesses have categorically stated that the curd was of Cow's milk.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text:
I find that no suggestion has been made to the Food Inspector that he was informed that the curd was made from Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195818333/
1
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: Cow's milk, but at the same time it was the duty of the Food Inspector to have enquired whether the curd was made from Cow's milk or Buffalo's milk.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: The difference would be, that as per entry A.11.01.11 in the Appendix B of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, for the State of Rajasthan for Buffalo Milk fat content has to be 5% and Milk solids not fat has to be 9%.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: For Cow milk, the standard would be 3.5% and 8.5% respectively.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text:
7. As noted above the curd had fat content of 5.02% and milk solids not fat 7.86%.
8.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: On the issue whether the courts below looked at the evidence concerning churning of the curd sample, for the reason (3 of 4) [CRLR-182/1996] the curd needs to be churned on account of the fact that fat tends to accumulate at the surface and other solids towards the bottom when milk cuddles into curd. In this connection I find that in response to a Court question the Inspector said that he churned the sample after lifting the same from the receptacle in which the curd was stored.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: But this is in direct conflict with what he has recorded in the report Ex.P8, in which he has written that the entire curd lying in the container was first churned and thereafter 600 grams sample was purchased.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 9. The defence witnesses have categorically disposed that the curd was manufactured from Cow's milk.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: The prescribed standard would require milk solid not fat to be 8.5%.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: The Public Analyst report finds the same to be 7.86%.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: Fat content as noted above is above the prescribed limit and would conform to law.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 10. Being a statute which attracts minimum sentence and attracts absolute liability, strict proof through credible evidence must be led by the prosecution.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 11. In the instant case the evidence concerning lifting of the sample and its churning being shaky entitles the petitioner to the benefit of doubt and I note that this critical aspect of the matter has been ignored by the learned trial Judge as well as the appellate Judge.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 12. The revision petition is disposed of, acquitting the petitioner of the charge for having committed an offence punishable under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: The impugned decision and the sentence imposed are quashed.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text: 13. The bail bond and surety bonds furnished by the petitioner (4 of 4) [CRLR-182/1996] are discharged.
sentences._hearing_file: Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017.json

sentences.text:
(PRADEEP NANDRAJOG)CJ.

Anoop Singh vs Pp on 4 July, 2017
Author: Chief Justice Bench: Chief Justice HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT JODHPUR S.B. Criminal Revision No. 182 / 1996 Anoop Singh Son of Shri Raghunath Singh Rajpurohit resident of Mathaniya District Jodhpur.
(At present lodged at Central Jail, Jodhpur)
----Petitioner Versus State of Rajasthan ----Respondent _____________________________________________________ For Petitioner(s) : Mr.Sunil Mehta For Respondent(s) : Mr.J.P.S.Choudhary, Public Prosecutor ___________________________________________________
__ HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE Judgment 04/07/2017
opennyai_summary.4_July_2017__ANALYSIS:
Cow's milk, but at the same time it was the duty of the Food Inspector to have enquired whether the curd was made from Cow's milk or Buffalo's milk.
The difference would be, that as per entry A.11.01.11 in the Appendix B of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, for the State of Rajasthan for Buffalo Milk fat content has to be 5% and Milk solids not fat has to be 9%.
The prescribed standard would require milk solid not fat to be 8.5%.
The Public Analyst report finds the same to be 7.86%.
Fat content as noted above is above the prescribed limit and would conform to law.
10. Being a statute which attracts minimum sentence and attracts absolute liability, strict proof through credible evidence must be led by the prosecution.
11. In the instant case the evidence concerning lifting of the sample and its churning being shaky entitles the petitioner to the benefit of doubt and I note that this critical aspect of the matter has been ignored by the learned trial Judge as well as the appellate Judge.
opennyai_summary.4_July_2017__decision:
12. The revision petition is disposed of, acquitting the petitioner of the charge for having committed an offence punishable under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The impugned decision and the sentence imposed are quashed.
13. The bail bond and surety bonds furnished by the petitioner (4 of 4) [CRLR-182/1996] are discharged.
